subject: Linguistics
title: Script and Identity
description: A quick, practical guide to Script and Identity.

hook.text: Serbia and Croatia speak nearly the same language—but Serbia uses Cyrillic and Croatia uses Latin.

buildup.text: Script choice often signals national, religious, or ethnic identity rather than linguistic necessity.

discovery.text: When Turkey switched from Arabic to Latin script in 1928, it was a political statement about modernization.

twist.text: Mongolia is shifting back from Cyrillic to its traditional script—a reassertion of cultural identity.

climax.text: Scripts carry symbolic power beyond their practical function—they mark who you are.

punchline.text: The alphabet you choose is a flag you wave.

quiz.question: Why did Turkey switch from Arabic to Latin script?
options: As a political statement about modernization
